summary: Lucas Goeller, a 10-year-old Pittsburgh boy born with biliary atresia, received a first liver transplant at age 2 but his transplanted liver is now failing, so he needs a second donation. His family has launched the "Save Lucas" campaign to find a donor and raise organ donation awareness. UPMC's Dr. George Mazariegos explains the challenges children face on transplant lists, including allocation problems and limited center capacity.
one_line: Ten-year-old Lucas Goeller of Pittsburgh, whose first transplanted liver is failing, needs a second transplant, and his family is campaigning for donors and awareness.
key_facts: Lucas Goeller, now 10, was born with biliary atresia, a blockage that prevents bile from traveling from the liver to the gallbladder.
In July 2015, at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, 2-year-old Lucas received the liver of 3-year-old Olivia Swedberg, who died of brain cancer a day earlier.
Lucas spent 18 months on the liver transplant list without receiving a single organ donation offer before the first transplant.
His mother Jessica Goeller started a Facebook page that led to a viral national campaign and attracted the attention of a Nebraska family.
After the first transplant, Lucas had "eight beautiful years" of a normal life before routine scans and blood work this year showed his liver failing.
His failing liver is affecting his lung function and ammonia levels, according to Jessica Goeller.
The ideal living donor for Lucas has type O blood, is aged 20 to 49, and has a BMI below 30.
Dr. George Mazariegos, chief of pediatric transplantation at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, says there are 10 times as many adults as children on the liver transplant list.

Dozens of children in the U.S. die each year while awaiting a new liver; Mazariegos aims to reduce this "wait list mortality" through partial liver transplants that split one liver between two recipients.
In 2018, UPMC started the Starzl Network for Excellence in Pediatric Transplantation, named for Dr. Thomas Starzl, to extend transplant expertise to other centers.
In Pennsylvania 18 children are waiting for liver transplants, and 300 children are on the list nationwide.
More than 100,000 individuals are on the organ donor list; Lucas has three brothers aged 12, 8, and 4.
